purpose: Provide a session-bounded, evaluable decision ontology for adopting and trusting LLMs/AI appropriately: choosing when (not) to use an LLM, selecting prompt/RAG/fine-tune/tools, knowing failure modes (hallucination, brittleness, bias, context/cutoff limits, overconfidence), interpreting evaluation, and applying safety and governance basics.
assumptions: This subdomain is modeled as a knowledge-searcher node about where/how to decide whether and how to use AI/LLMs and trust their outputs.
Nodes are concrete decision work-units for adopting AI, each bounded to one heavy-thinking session.
No observed dataset, expert-judgment, or benchmark evidence was supplied; all values are heuristic priors.
Provider-agnostic LLM practice is assumed; where a provider matters it is treated as a configuration, not a node.
Key texts (Russell & Norvig; Huyen) inform heuristic priors but are not cited as measured evidence.
exclusions: model internals, architecture, and training mechanics in depth
vendor- or model-specific pricing, APIs, or version numbers
general software/MLOps engineering not specific to LLM limits and trust
deep alignment research beyond practitioner-level basics
data labeling and dataset construction methodology in depth

competency_questions.question: For a given task, is an LLM the right tool, or should a rule, classical ML, search, or a human be used instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USE_CASE_FIT_TRIAGE yields a fit decision with a named baseline

competency_questions.question: Should this task use prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, or a combination, and at what cost/latency/quality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADOPTION_PATH_CHOICE and COST_LATENCY_QUALITY_TRADEOFF yield a path with cost estimate

competency_questions.question: Where is fabrication (hallucination) costly enough to require grounding or verification?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HALLUCINATION_RISK_ASSESS yields a risk rating and grounding requirement

competency_questions.question: How brittle or overconfident is the model on this task, and what perturbation/calibration tests bound it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROMPT_SENSITIVITY_BRITTLENESS and OVERCONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION yield tests and thresholds

competency_questions.question: What bias, alignment, and fairness risks does this use case carry for affected people?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BIAS_FAIRNESS_ASSESS and ALIGNMENT_BASICS yield assessments and mitigations

competency_questions.question: How should current and large knowledge be supplied: retrieval, long context, or tools, given context and cutoff limits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RAG_VS_LONG_CONTEXT, STALE_KNOWLEDGE_CUTOFF, CONTEXT_LENGTH_LIMITS yield a grounding strategy

competency_questions.question: When should tools or guardrails be added, and how is untrusted input defended against?
What does a given evaluation or benchmark score actually mean for this deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_DESIGN, BENCHMARK_INTERPRETATION, LLM_AS_JUDGE, CONTAMINATION_CONTROL yield interpretation

competency_questions.question: Which decisions require human review based on risk, irreversibility, and confidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUMAN_IN_THE_LOOP yields review routing tied to thresholds

competency_questions.question: How is the deployed system monitored for drift, brittleness, and silent regression?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MONITORING_DRIFT and CONTEXT_LENGTH_LIMITS and PROMPT_SENSITIVITY_BRITTLENESS yield monitoring

competency_questions.question: Does the chosen evaluation predict production performance, and is it contamination-free?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_DESIGN, BENCHMARK_INTERPRETATION, CONTAMINATION_CONTROL establish predictive, clean eval

competency_questions.question: What is the cost/latency/quality operating point and when should it be revisited?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_LATENCY_QUALITY_TRADEOFF yields an operating point and revisit triggers

competency_questions.question: How is data handled, who is accountable, and what is the rollback path when AI causes harm?
After a model or prompt change, how is quality re-verified and responsibility maintained?

glossary.definition: a model output that is fluent and plausible but factually false or fabricated
retrieval-augmented generation: grounding model output in retrieved external documents
further training a model on task data to learn new behavior or style
the finite number of tokens a model can attend to at once
the date after which the model has no parametric knowledge of events
the match between a model's expressed confidence and its actual accuracy
using an LLM to grade or rank other model outputs
leakage of test data into training data that inflates evaluation scores
an attack where untrusted content overrides instructions or exfiltrates data
an input/output control that filters or validates model interaction for safety or format
the degree to which a model acts according to the operator's true intent rather than a proxy
a workflow where a human reviews, approves, or overrides model output
the minimum acceptable quality level the system must hold while optimizing cost/latency

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established AI practice and texts (Russell & Norvig 'Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach'; Huyen 'Designing Machine Learning Systems') and applied-LLM engineering practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: observed model accuracy or hallucination rates
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Decide whether a task is a fit for an LLM at all versus a deterministic rule, classical ML, search, or a human, before any model work begins.
contradictors: builder who uses an LLM for every task by default
inputs: task description and required output guarantees

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deterministic or cheaper non-LLM method is shown to meet the requirement

pros.claim: a fit screen prevents using an LLM where a rule is cheaper, exact, and auditable
pros.example: routing a tax calculation to deterministic code, not an LLM

pros.claim: naming a baseline makes the LLM's marginal value measurable
pros.example: comparing an LLM classifier to a logistic-regression baseline

cons.claim: over-screening can reject LLMs from tasks where they would have excelled
cons.example: rejecting an LLM for triage that it handles better than rules

cons.claim: requirements are often vague at triage time
cons.example: choosing before auditability needs are known

failure_modes: LLM chosen for a task needing exact arithmetic or auditability
no baseline compared, so value of the LLM is unknown
reaching for an LLM because it is novel, not because it fits
acceptance_tests: a non-LLM baseline (rules/ML/search/human) is named and compared
the task tolerates probabilistic, non-exact output
a stop rule says when NOT to use an LLM
revisit_triggers: a rules or ML baseline beats the LLM

nodes.definition: Choose the adaptation path for an LLM task: prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning, or a combination, given knowledge needs and constraints.
contradictors: engineer who fine-tunes first for every gap
inputs: need for new facts vs new behavior/style
budget for data, compute, and maintenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dynamic or proprietary knowledge needs make retrieval dominate prompting

pros.claim: matching path to knowledge profile avoids paying fine-tune cost for a retrieval problem
pros.example: using RAG for changing policy docs instead of re-training

pros.claim: a fallback ladder forces trying cheap prompting before costly training
pros.example: prompt, then RAG, then fine-tune only if needed

cons.claim: paths are not exclusive; over-simple choice ignores hybrids
cons.example: treating RAG and fine-tune as either/or when both help

cons.claim: path estimates are uncertain before a prototype
cons.example: guessing fine-tune quality without a pilot

failure_modes: fine-tuning when the need is fresh facts (should be RAG)
RAG bolted on where prompting suffices
fine-tuning chosen for a behavior describable in a prompt
acceptance_tests: the decision states why prompt OR RAG OR fine-tune fits the knowledge profile
a cheaper path was tried before a costlier one
cost/latency/quality of each candidate path is estimated
revisit_triggers: style/format must be learned not described
fine-tune data becomes available or stale

nodes.definition: Decide between retrieval-augmented grounding and stuffing more into the context window, weighing relevance, cost, latency, and context-length limits.

excluded: whether to use RAG at all (path choice)

contradictors: engineer who assumes bigger context always wins
outputs: grounding strategy (retrieve vs stuff vs hybrid)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus grows past what fits or stays useful in the context window

pros.claim: retrieval keeps only relevant context, controlling cost and attention dilution
pros.example: retrieving 5 relevant chunks instead of a 300-page manual

pros.claim: explicit context budgeting exposes the finite, priced nature of long context
pros.example: capping injected tokens to hold latency

cons.claim: retrieval adds a pipeline and its own failure modes
cons.example: a bad retriever surfaces irrelevant passages

cons.claim: some tasks genuinely need broad context that retrieval fragments
cons.example: reasoning across a whole contract

failure_modes: dumping a whole corpus into context and degrading attention
retrieving low-relevance chunks that dilute the answer
ignoring that long context still has a finite, costly limit
acceptance_tests: the choice accounts for corpus size vs context limit
retrieval relevance is measured, not assumed
lost-in-the-middle / position effects are considered

nodes.definition: Decide when to give an LLM external tools (calculators, code, search, APIs) versus relying on the model's parametric ability, to fix specific weaknesses.
contradictors: builder who adds every available tool reflexively

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a known weakness (math, fresh facts, exact lookup) is identified that a tool removes

pros.claim: offloading math/lookup to deterministic tools removes a whole hallucination class
pros.example: a calculator tool eliminates arithmetic errors

pros.claim: mapping tools to weaknesses keeps the tool surface minimal
pros.example: adding only a search tool because recency is the gap

cons.claim: each tool adds latency, failure surface, and validation burden
cons.example: a flaky API stalls the whole chain

cons.claim: tool outputs can themselves be wrong or stale
cons.example: a search tool returning an outdated figure

failure_modes: adding tools that the model rarely needs, raising latency
trusting tool output without validating it
using the model to do arithmetic a calculator should do
acceptance_tests: each added tool maps to a specific model weakness it fixes
tool outputs are validated before being trusted
a no-tool baseline is compared
revisit_triggers: a new model weakness or hallucination class appears
a deterministic tool can replace a guessed answer

nodes.definition: Estimate and bound the risk that the model fabricates plausible-but-false content for a given task, and set grounding and verification requirements.
contradictors: user who trusts fluent output as factual
inputs: task domain and cost of a false statement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the task moves into a domain where fabrication is high-cost (legal, medical, factual citation)

pros.claim: rating fabrication cost focuses grounding where it matters
pros.example: requiring citations for medical claims but not brainstorms

pros.claim: a verification step catches invented facts before they ship
pros.example: checking each cited case actually exists

cons.claim: grounding and verification add latency and cost
cons.example: every claim cross-checked slows a chat assistant

cons.claim: hallucination cannot be driven to zero, only bounded
cons.example: a grounded model still occasionally invents detail

failure_modes: confident citation of nonexistent sources
plausible but invented facts accepted as true
no grounding where fabrication is costly
acceptance_tests: fabrication-cost of the task is rated
grounding or citation is required where cost is high
a verification step is specified for unverifiable claims
revisit_triggers: task enters a high-stakes factual domain

nodes.definition: Characterize how much outputs swing with small prompt, ordering, or phrasing changes, and harden prompts and pipelines against that brittleness.
contradictors: author who assumes one good prompt run generalizes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: output varies materially under paraphrase, option reordering, or formatting change

pros.claim: perturbation testing exposes hidden fragility before users do
pros.example: reordering MCQ options reveals a position bias

pros.claim: constrained formats reduce variance in production
pros.example: forcing JSON output to stabilize parsing

cons.claim: perturbation suites add test-engineering cost
cons.example: maintaining paraphrase sets per prompt

cons.claim: over-constraining can reduce useful flexibility
cons.example: rigid templates failing on edge inputs

failure_modes: answer flips when answer options are reordered
a working prompt breaks after a model update
format drift across otherwise-identical inputs
acceptance_tests: outputs are tested under paraphrase and option-order perturbation
variance under perturbation is bounded to a threshold
a fixed template or constrained format is used in production

nodes.definition: Account for the model's training cutoff and stale parametric knowledge, deciding where freshness is required and how to supply current information.
contradictors: user who treats the model as an up-to-date oracle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a task depends on facts that changed after the model's training cutoff

pros.claim: explicit cutoff-awareness prevents trusting the model on recent events
pros.example: routing 'who won yesterday' to search, not parametric memory

pros.claim: a freshness plan supplies current facts where they matter
pros.example: injecting today's price via a tool

cons.claim: freshness routing adds pipeline complexity
cons.example: deciding per-query whether retrieval is needed

cons.claim: cutoff boundaries are fuzzy, not a hard line
cons.example: partial knowledge of near-cutoff events

failure_modes: trusting the model on recent events it cannot know
assuming the cutoff is later than it is
no freshness path for time-sensitive facts
acceptance_tests: the task's freshness requirement is stated against the model cutoff
fresh facts are supplied via retrieval or tools where needed
the model is not asked to know post-cutoff events unaided

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate social, representational, and task biases in model outputs that could cause unfair or skewed decisions for affected groups.
contradictors: builder who reports only aggregate accuracy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the system informs decisions about people or protected groups

pros.claim: group-disaggregated testing surfaces harm that averages hide
pros.example: checking acceptance rates per demographic, not overall

pros.claim: stated fairness criteria make tradeoffs explicit and reviewable
pros.example: declaring equal-opportunity as the target

cons.claim: fairness definitions conflict and cannot all be satisfied
cons.example: equalized odds vs demographic parity tension

cons.claim: group test data may be scarce or sensitive
cons.example: too few samples per subgroup to measure

failure_modes: skewed outputs disadvantaging a group
average metrics hiding subgroup harm
amplifying biases present in training data
acceptance_tests: bias is tested across relevant groups, not just on average
a mitigation or human-review path exists for affected decisions
fairness criteria for the use case are stated

nodes.definition: Assess whether the model's expressed confidence matches its accuracy and add calibration, abstention, or uncertainty signaling where overconfidence is costly.
contradictors: user who reads confident phrasing as truth
inputs: stakes of acting on the answer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: users act on confidently-worded answers in high-stakes settings

pros.claim: calibration checks separate confidence from correctness
pros.example: finding the model is 90% sure but 60% right

pros.claim: an abstention path lets the system decline instead of guessing
pros.example: returning 'insufficient information' when unsure

cons.claim: calibration data is costly to collect
cons.example: needing labeled accuracy to measure calibration

cons.claim: too much abstention reduces usefulness
cons.example: a model that declines too often

failure_modes: fluent, confident, and wrong
no abstention so the model always answers
users equate fluency with reliability
acceptance_tests: confidence vs accuracy is checked, not assumed
an abstention or 'I don't know' path exists for low-confidence cases
fluent tone is not treated as evidence of correctness
revisit_triggers: stakes of acting on output rise

nodes.definition: Manage the finite context window: truncation, lost-in-the-middle degradation, and compression loss, and design inputs to stay within reliable limits.
contradictors: engineer who assumes the full window is uniformly reliable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: inputs approach or exceed the reliable portion of the context window

pros.claim: context budgeting prevents silent truncation of instructions
pros.example: reserving tokens for the system prompt

pros.claim: ordering critical content avoids lost-in-the-middle loss
pros.example: placing the question first and last

cons.claim: budgeting constrains how much can be supplied at once
cons.example: dropping useful but lower-priority context

cons.claim: position effects vary by model and are hard to predict
cons.example: a placement that helps one model hurts another

failure_modes: silent truncation dropping key instructions
important facts buried mid-context and ignored
compression summaries losing required detail
acceptance_tests: input length is checked against the reliable context budget
critical content is placed to avoid lost-in-the-middle loss
truncation/compression loss is detected and handled
revisit_triggers: input length grows toward the window limit

nodes.definition: Design a task-relevant evaluation: choose metrics, datasets, and decision thresholds that actually predict production performance for this use case.
contradictors: builder who reports a public-benchmark number as the product metric

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the production task diverges from what the chosen eval measures

pros.claim: a task-matched eval predicts production behavior, not a proxy
pros.example: evaluating a summarizer on the actual document type it serves

pros.claim: tying metrics to decisions prevents optimizing a meaningless score
pros.example: using cost-weighted error, not raw accuracy

cons.claim: good eval data is expensive to build and label
cons.example: hand-labeling a representative test set

cons.claim: metrics always simplify a richer real objective
cons.example: a single score hiding multi-dimensional quality

failure_modes: optimizing a metric that does not predict real performance
eval task mismatched to deployment
tiny or unrepresentative eval set
acceptance_tests: the eval task matches the production task
metrics are tied to the decision the eval informs
a held-out, task-representative dataset is used
revisit_triggers: use case shifts from the eval's task
new failure modes appear in production

nodes.definition: Interpret what a benchmark score does and does not mean: scope, ceiling effects, distribution shift, and the gap between leaderboard and real-task performance.
contradictors: buyer who picks a model by a single leaderboard number
inputs: benchmark scores and their task definitions
outputs: interpretation of score meaning and limits

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark score is being used to justify a deployment decision

pros.claim: stating what a score excludes prevents over-reading a rank
pros.example: noting a coding benchmark says nothing about safety

pros.claim: benchmark-to-task gap analysis predicts real-world drop
pros.example: expecting lower accuracy off the benchmark distribution

cons.claim: careful interpretation slows fast model comparison
cons.example: resisting a quick 'X beats Y' claim

cons.claim: limitation analysis needs benchmark-internals knowledge
cons.example: knowing how a benchmark was constructed

failure_modes: treating a leaderboard rank as fitness for the real task
ignoring saturation/ceiling effects
comparing scores across incomparable settings
acceptance_tests: the benchmark's task scope is compared to the real task
what the score does NOT measure is stated
distribution shift from benchmark to deployment is considered
revisit_triggers: a benchmark is cited for a deployment decision

nodes.definition: Decide when and how to use an LLM to grade other model outputs, controlling judge bias, position effects, and self-preference, and validating against human labels.
contradictors: team that trusts judge scores without human validation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an LLM judge is used to make accept/reject or ranking decisions at scale

pros.claim: validating against human labels keeps automated judging honest
pros.example: checking judge-human agreement before scaling

pros.claim: bias controls (swapping order, blind models) reduce systematic error
pros.example: randomizing option order to cancel position bias

cons.claim: judges inherit the biases and blind spots of LLMs
cons.example: a judge missing the same errors the generator makes

cons.claim: validation sampling adds human-labeling cost
cons.example: hand-grading a sample to calibrate the judge

failure_modes: judge favoring its own model family (self-preference)
position bias toward the first option
scoring fluency over correctness
acceptance_tests: judge scores are validated against human labels on a sample
position/verbosity/self-preference biases are mitigated
the judge's failure modes are documented

nodes.definition: Detect and control train/test contamination so eval scores reflect generalization rather than memorization of leaked test data.
contradictors: evaluator who reuses old public benchmarks uncritically

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a public benchmark may have leaked into the model's training data

pros.claim: fresh or held-out tests separate memorization from generalization
pros.example: using a post-cutoff test set to avoid leakage

pros.claim: contamination assessment caveats scores that cannot be trusted
pros.example: flagging a saturated public benchmark

cons.claim: detecting contamination is hard without training-data access
cons.example: unknown training corpora block certainty

cons.claim: building fresh tests repeatedly is costly
cons.example: new held-out sets each cycle

failure_modes: high score from memorized test items
public benchmark leaked into training
trusting a contaminated score as generalization
acceptance_tests: contamination risk of the benchmark is assessed
a fresh or held-out test reduces leakage risk
anomalously high scores are investigated
revisit_triggers: a public benchmark is used for a key decision
model training data provenance is unknown

nodes.definition: Balance model quality against cost and latency: choose model size, routing, caching, and quality floors that meet requirements at acceptable cost.
contradictors: builder who always picks the largest model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cost or latency budgets change, or a smaller model meets the quality floor

pros.claim: a defined quality floor prevents cost cuts from degrading the product
pros.example: holding accuracy >= 0.9 while minimizing cost

pros.claim: routing cheap models for easy queries cuts cost without quality loss
pros.example: small model for FAQs, large for hard cases

cons.claim: the floor itself depends on a trustworthy eval
cons.example: a wrong eval lets quality slip unnoticed

cons.claim: routing adds system complexity
cons.example: a misrouted hard query degrading answers

failure_modes: cutting cost below the quality floor
optimizing latency and silently dropping quality
using a frontier model where a small one suffices
acceptance_tests: a measured quality floor is defined before optimizing cost
cost and latency are measured against that floor
routing/caching tradeoffs are evaluated, not assumed
revisit_triggers: a cheaper model meets the quality floor

nodes.definition: Design input and output guardrails (filters, validators, refusals, schema checks) that catch unsafe, off-policy, or malformed responses before they reach users.
contradictors: builder who ships raw model output unfiltered

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the system can emit unsafe, off-policy, or malformed output to a user

pros.claim: output guardrails catch unsafe content before it reaches users
pros.example: blocking a harmful instruction the model produced

pros.claim: schema validators reject malformed output that would break downstream
pros.example: rejecting non-JSON before parsing

cons.claim: guardrails over-block and frustrate legitimate use
cons.example: refusing a benign medical question

cons.claim: attackers adapt; guardrails need continual updating
cons.example: a new jailbreak slipping past filters

failure_modes: unsafe output reaching users
jailbreaks bypassing filters
over-blocking legitimate requests
acceptance_tests: unsafe/off-policy output classes are enumerated and filtered
guardrails are tested against known jailbreak/abuse patterns
malformed-output validation exists where structure is required
revisit_triggers: a new abuse or jailbreak pattern appears

nodes.definition: Defend against prompt injection and untrusted-content attacks where retrieved or user data overrides instructions or exfiltrates data through tools.
contradictors: builder who trusts retrieved/user text as instructions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the model processes untrusted content (web, documents, user data) with tool or data access

pros.claim: isolating untrusted content stops it from hijacking instructions
pros.example: treating retrieved text as data, never as commands

pros.claim: least-privilege tooling limits exfiltration damage
pros.example: a read-only tool that cannot send data out

cons.claim: perfect isolation is hard when content must influence behavior
cons.example: a summarizer must read the very text that may attack it

cons.claim: tight permissions can block legitimate workflows
cons.example: a needed action blocked by least-privilege

failure_modes: retrieved text overriding system instructions
data exfiltration via tool calls
injected instructions in user-supplied documents
acceptance_tests: untrusted content is isolated from trusted instructions
tool/data permissions follow least privilege
injection attempts are tested against the pipeline
revisit_triggers: new untrusted data sources are ingested
a new injection technique is reported

nodes.definition: Govern how user and proprietary data is collected, sent to models, retained, and used for training, meeting privacy and data-handling obligations.
contradictors: builder who pipes raw user data to any API

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: personal or proprietary data is sent to or retained by a model provider

pros.claim: data minimization shrinks the blast radius of any leak
pros.example: stripping PII before the model call

pros.claim: knowing retention/training terms prevents silent data reuse
pros.example: choosing a no-train endpoint for sensitive data

cons.claim: redaction can remove context the model needs
cons.example: masking a name that mattered for the task

cons.claim: compliance varies by jurisdiction and is moving
cons.example: rules differing across regions

failure_modes: sending PII to a provider that retains/trains on it
no redaction of sensitive fields
unclear data-residency obligations
acceptance_tests: data sent to the model is minimized and classified by sensitivity
retention and training-use terms are known and acceptable
a redaction or on-prem path exists for sensitive data

nodes.definition: Decide where humans must review, approve, or override model output based on risk, irreversibility, and confidence, and design the review workflow.
contradictors: builder who automates irreversible decisions end-to-end

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model output drives a high-risk or irreversible decision

pros.claim: routing high-risk decisions to humans bounds worst-case harm
pros.example: a human approves any automated account closure

pros.claim: threshold-based triggers focus scarce review where it matters
pros.example: escalating only low-confidence, high-stakes cases

cons.claim: review adds latency and cost and can bottleneck
cons.example: a queue of approvals slowing throughput

cons.claim: rubber-stamp review gives false assurance
cons.example: reviewers approving without reading

failure_modes: full automation of an irreversible high-risk decision
rubber-stamp review that adds no safety
review bottleneck that gets bypassed
acceptance_tests: high-risk and irreversible decisions route to a human
review triggers are tied to risk/confidence thresholds
reviewers can effectively override the model
revisit_triggers: model confidence on a class drops

nodes.definition: Apply alignment fundamentals (instruction-following, refusal behavior, RLHF/preference shaping, specification gaming) to judge whether a model will act as intended.
contradictors: builder who assumes the model simply does what is asked
outputs: alignment-risk notes for the use case

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the model's objective or refusal behavior may diverge from the operator's intent

pros.claim: examining the intent-objective gap anticipates specification gaming
pros.example: foreseeing a metric being gamed rather than satisfied

pros.claim: checking refusal behavior catches over- and under-refusal early
pros.example: finding the model refuses a benign safety question

cons.claim: alignment is partially understood; assessments are uncertain
cons.example: no guarantee the proxy matches intent

cons.claim: refusal calibration trades safety against helpfulness
cons.example: tightening refusals reduces usefulness

failure_modes: model optimizing a proxy that diverges from intent
over-refusal blocking legitimate use
under-refusal enabling misuse
acceptance_tests: the gap between specified objective and true intent is examined
refusal and over-refusal behavior is checked against policy
reward-hacking / specification-gaming risks are noted

nodes.definition: Monitor a deployed LLM system for quality drift, distribution shift, new failure modes, and silent regressions after model or prompt changes.
contradictors: team that ships a model change without re-evaluating

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a model/prompt change or input-distribution shift could silently degrade quality

pros.claim: monitoring against a baseline catches silent regressions fast
pros.example: an alert when accuracy drops after a model swap

pros.claim: change-triggered re-eval prevents blind upgrades
pros.example: re-running the eval suite on every version bump

cons.claim: monitoring infrastructure is real engineering cost
cons.example: building dashboards and alert pipelines

cons.claim: noisy alerts cause fatigue and get ignored
cons.example: too many low-value drift alerts

failure_modes: silent regression after a model update
input drift degrading quality unnoticed
no rollback path when quality drops
acceptance_tests: live quality and failure signals are monitored against a baseline
model/prompt version changes trigger re-evaluation
drift and regression alerts have owners and thresholds
revisit_triggers: a new failure mode is reported

nodes.definition: Establish accountability, documentation, decision records, and rollback authority for AI use, so that responsibility and recourse are clear when things go wrong.
contradictors: org that deploys AI with no named owner

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an AI-driven decision causes harm and responsibility/recourse must be assignable

pros.claim: named accountability ensures recourse when AI causes harm
pros.example: a decision owner who can be held responsible

pros.claim: decision records make AI choices auditable after the fact
pros.example: logging which model/version made a call

cons.claim: governance overhead can slow legitimate deployment
cons.example: approval steps delaying low-risk pilots

cons.claim: documentation decays if not maintained
cons.example: stale model cards no one updates

failure_modes: no one accountable when an AI decision causes harm
undocumented model and prompt versions
no rollback authority in an incident
acceptance_tests: each AI-influenced decision class has a named accountable owner
decision records and model/version documentation exist
a rollback/kill authority and path are defined
revisit_triggers: ownership of an AI system changes

edges.why_related: fit must be settled before choosing an adaptation path
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing a path for an ill-fit task wastes it
edges.example: deciding prompt-vs-RAG only after the LLM is the right tool
edges.resolution_rule: settle fit before path

edges.why_related: the chosen task defines the cost of fabrication
edges.risk_of_conflict: assessing hallucination for the wrong task misallocates effort
edges.example: rating fabrication cost once the task is fixed
edges.resolution_rule: fix task before grounding plan

edges.why_related: the task defines which unsafe output classes matter
edges.risk_of_conflict: generic guardrails miss task-specific risks
edges.example: filtering only the unsafe classes the task can emit
edges.resolution_rule: define task before guardrails

edges.why_related: the task determines what data flows to the model
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-broad data flows raise privacy risk
edges.example: sending only fields the task requires
edges.resolution_rule: scope data flow to the task

edges.why_related: task weaknesses determine which tools help
edges.risk_of_conflict: adding tools before knowing the weakness
edges.example: mapping tools to the task's gaps
edges.resolution_rule: know the task before adding tools

edges.why_related: the task and its affected people set fairness needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: assessing bias without the affected population
edges.example: testing groups the task actually impacts
edges.resolution_rule: fix task and population first

edges.why_related: choosing RAG opens the retrieve-vs-stuff sub-decision
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning retrieval before deciding to use RAG
edges.example: deciding chunking only after RAG is chosen
edges.resolution_rule: decide path before retrieval detail

edges.why_related: the adaptation path sets the cost/latency envelope
edges.risk_of_conflict: costing a path before it is chosen
edges.example: estimating serving cost for the selected path
edges.resolution_rule: choose path before costing it

edges.why_related: a task-relevant eval frames what benchmark scores mean here
edges.benefit_of_coupling: benchmarks read against the real task
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading benchmarks with no task-relevant eval
edges.example: comparing a leaderboard to the eval's task
edges.resolution_rule: build eval before reading benchmarks

edges.why_related: the eval task and rubric define what a judge must grade
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing a judge with no eval target
edges.example: grading against the eval rubric
edges.resolution_rule: define eval before judge

edges.why_related: eval data choice determines contamination exposure
edges.risk_of_conflict: controlling contamination with no eval defined
edges.example: choosing fresh data inside eval design
edges.resolution_rule: design eval before contamination control

edges.why_related: the eval sets the quality floor that bounds cost cuts
edges.risk_of_conflict: cutting cost with no measured floor
edges.example: holding eval-defined accuracy while minimizing cost
edges.resolution_rule: measure quality before trading it for cost

edges.why_related: the offline eval provides the baseline production is monitored against
edges.benefit_of_coupling: drift measured vs a real baseline
edges.risk_of_conflict: monitoring with no baseline to compare to
edges.example: alerting when live metrics fall below the eval baseline
edges.resolution_rule: establish eval baseline before monitoring

edges.why_related: high fabrication cost forces human review
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating high-fabrication-cost output
edges.example: routing unverifiable high-stakes claims to a human
edges.resolution_rule: assess fabrication risk before automating

edges.why_related: low-confidence cases are the ones to escalate
edges.risk_of_conflict: escalating without a confidence signal
edges.example: sending low-confidence outputs to review
edges.resolution_rule: get confidence signal before routing review

edges.why_related: baseline guardrails are the substrate injection defense extends
edges.risk_of_conflict: building injection defense with no guardrails
edges.example: layering isolation on top of output filters
edges.resolution_rule: stand up guardrails before injection defense

edges.why_related: giving tools creates the exfiltration surface to defend
edges.risk_of_conflict: granting tools with no injection defense
edges.example: applying least privilege to the tools added
edges.resolution_rule: decide tools before securing them

edges.why_related: review routing defines who is accountable for each decision
edges.risk_of_conflict: assigning accountability with no review design
edges.example: naming the owner of each reviewed decision
edges.resolution_rule: design review before assigning accountability

edges.why_related: data-handling obligations feed accountability records
edges.risk_of_conflict: accountability with no data-handling policy
edges.example: documenting data decisions in the governance record
edges.resolution_rule: set data policy before accountability records

edges.why_related: the finite context window bounds how much can be stuffed
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the window inflates the stuff option
edges.example: capping injected tokens to the reliable window
edges.resolution_rule: retrieval wins when content exceeds the reliable window

edges.why_related: freshness needs constrain reliance on parametric knowledge
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring cutoff trusts stale parametric facts
edges.example: routing post-cutoff facts to retrieval
edges.resolution_rule: supply fresh facts externally when cutoff blocks them

edges.why_related: truncation and lost-in-the-middle raise fabrication probability
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded context silently dropping facts
edges.example: a buried instruction ignored, inducing a made-up answer
edges.resolution_rule: detect truncation; re-ground when context is lost

edges.why_related: brittleness inflates eval variance and harms reliability
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval that ignores prompt variance
edges.example: an eval score that swings with phrasing
edges.resolution_rule: include perturbation tests in the eval

edges.why_related: stale knowledge causes confident wrong claims about recent facts
edges.risk_of_conflict: trusting parametric recall for recent events
edges.example: an invented recent statistic
edges.resolution_rule: ground recent facts to cut stale-fact fabrication

edges.why_related: mis-read benchmarks distort the quality estimate in cost tradeoffs
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a model on a misleading rank
edges.example: over-paying for a model that benchmarks well but underperforms
edges.resolution_rule: use task-relevant quality, not raw benchmark rank

edges.why_related: contamination inflates scores and corrupts interpretation
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading a contaminated score as real skill
edges.example: a memorized benchmark inflating a rank
edges.resolution_rule: discount or re-test contaminated benchmarks

edges.why_related: alignment gaps (over/under refusal) shape what guardrails must cover
edges.risk_of_conflict: guardrails blind to refusal behavior
edges.example: under-refusal letting misuse through
edges.resolution_rule: extend guardrails to cover refusal-behavior gaps

edges.why_related: production drift signals trigger revisiting the eval
edges.risk_of_conflict: an eval that never updates with reality
edges.example: new failure modes prompting an eval refresh
edges.resolution_rule: revisit eval when monitoring finds eval-production gaps; stop when re-eval shows no gap

edges.why_related: observed fabrication in production reopens the risk assessment
edges.risk_of_conflict: a one-time risk rating going stale
edges.example: logged hallucinations raising the risk rating
edges.resolution_rule: re-assess hallucination risk on observed fabrication; stop when grounding holds

edges.why_related: reviewer overrides are a signal of model quality drift
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring override patterns
edges.example: a spike in overrides flagging regression
edges.resolution_rule: feed override rates into monitoring; stop when override rate normalizes

edges.why_related: cost/latency pressure tempts cutting grounding that controls fabrication
edges.risk_of_conflict: cheaper, faster, and more hallucination-prone
edges.example: dropping a verification step to cut latency
edges.resolution_rule: grounding wins where fabrication cost is high; otherwise bounded cost cuts allowed

edges.why_related: review adds latency/cost that the tradeoff pressures away
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating away review to hit latency
edges.example: removing approval to speed throughput
edges.resolution_rule: for high-risk/irreversible decisions human review dominates cost/latency

edges.why_related: guardrail and validation steps add latency/cost
edges.risk_of_conflict: stripping guardrails for speed
edges.example: skipping output validation to save a call
edges.resolution_rule: safety guardrails dominate latency for unsafe-output classes

edges.why_related: more retrieval/context improves quality but raises cost and latency
edges.benefit_of_coupling: context budget chosen with cost in view
edges.risk_of_conflict: stuffing context that blows the latency budget
edges.example: injecting 50 chunks and doubling latency
edges.resolution_rule: retrieve the minimum context that meets the quality floor

edges.why_related: fine-tuning/RAG on sensitive data conflicts with data minimization
edges.risk_of_conflict: training on data that should not leave the org
edges.example: fine-tuning on raw user PII
edges.resolution_rule: privacy/minimization dominates path choice for sensitive data

edges.why_related: group fairness testing and mitigation add cost the tradeoff resists
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping subgroup testing to save effort
edges.example: reporting only aggregate accuracy to ship faster
edges.resolution_rule: fairness obligations dominate cost for people-affecting decisions

edges.why_related: both concern trusting output that may be wrong despite fluency
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating fabrication with miscalibration
edges.example: a confident invented fact is both
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: one is content truth, the other is confidence-accuracy match

edges.why_related: both temper trust in reported scores
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as one step
edges.example: a high score that is both mis-read and contaminated
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: interpretation vs leakage detection

edges.why_related: both protect against unwanted data exposure
edges.risk_of_conflict: merging security and privacy concerns
edges.example: exfiltration is both a security and privacy harm
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: attack defense vs data governance

conflict_axes.trigger: a cost or latency target pressures cutting grounding, verification, or model size below the quality floor
resolution_order: cut cost only above the floor
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the quality floor from the eval dominates; cost optimization is allowed only above it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: cost is cut below the measured quality floor
conflict_axes.example: dropping a verification step to hit a latency SLA

conflict_axes.trigger: throughput pressure pushes to automate a high-risk or irreversible decision
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for high-risk or irreversible decisions human review dominates automation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an irreversible decision is fully automated
conflict_axes.example: auto-closing accounts with no human approval

conflict_axes.trigger: a task needs current or exact facts the model's parametric memory cannot reliably supply
resolution_order: fall back to parametric only for stable knowledge
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: external grounding dominates for fresh or exact facts; parametric use is limited to stable knowledge
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: recent facts are answered from parametric memory
conflict_axes.example: answering today's price from training memory

conflict_axes.trigger: a public benchmark rank is used to justify a deployment decision
resolution_order: compare benchmark task to real task
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the task-relevant eval dominates a public leaderboard rank when they disagree
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a model is chosen on a leaderboard number alone
conflict_axes.example: buying a model purely on an MMLU rank

conflict_axes.trigger: tightening guardrails/refusals reduces unsafe output but also blocks legitimate use
resolution_order: prefer safety for genuinely unsafe classes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety dominates for genuinely unsafe output classes; helpfulness is preserved elsewhere
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: guardrails over-block benign requests at scale
conflict_axes.example: refusing all medical questions including safe ones

conflict_axes.trigger: more data sent to or trained into the model improves capability but raises privacy exposure
resolution_order: use no-train/on-prem paths for sensitive data
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: data minimization and privacy obligations dominate capability gains for sensitive data
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: PII is sent to a retain-and-train endpoint

conflict_axes.trigger: delivery pressure pushes to ship before the eval is trustworthy or monitoring is in place
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation rigor dominates ship speed for any production deployment
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a model change ships with no re-evaluation
conflict_axes.example: swapping models without re-running the eval

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing average accuracy can hide or worsen harm to a subgroup
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: subgroup fairness dominates aggregate accuracy for people-affecting decisions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: only aggregate metrics are reported for a people-affecting system
conflict_axes.example: shipping on overall accuracy while a subgroup is harmed

edge_cases.trigger: an LLM is chosen for a task needing exact, auditable output
edge_cases.failure_mode: probabilistic output where determinism was required
edge_cases.example: using an LLM to total an invoice
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether the task requires exact/auditable output and a baseline was compared
resolution: route exact tasks to deterministic code or a tool

edge_cases.trigger: a high-fabrication-cost task has no grounding
edge_cases.failure_mode: confident citation of a nonexistent source
edge_cases.example: citing a court case that does not exist
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each cited source resolves to a real artifact

edge_cases.trigger: a leaderboard rank is used as the product metric
edge_cases.failure_mode: model chosen that benchmarks well but underperforms on the real task
edge_cases.example: picking the top-MMLU model for a summarization product
edge_cases.detection_method: check that a task-relevant eval, not a public rank, drove the choice

edge_cases.trigger: a public benchmark may be in the training data
edge_cases.example: near-perfect score on a known leaked benchmark
edge_cases.detection_method: assess benchmark provenance and look for anomalous scores

edge_cases.trigger: an LLM judge drives decisions without human validation
edge_cases.example: ranking models with a judge that favors its own family
edge_cases.detection_method: require judge-vs-human agreement on a sample before scaling

edge_cases.trigger: untrusted content reaches a model with tool/data access
edge_cases.failure_mode: injected instructions override system prompt or exfiltrate data
edge_cases.example: a retrieved web page instructing the model to leak a secret
edge_cases.detection_method: test the pipeline against known injection payloads

edge_cases.trigger: sensitive data is sent to a retain-and-train provider
edge_cases.failure_mode: personal data retained or trained on without basis
edge_cases.example: sending raw customer records to a training endpoint
edge_cases.detection_method: audit data flows against sensitivity classification and provider terms

edge_cases.trigger: a model or prompt version changes with no re-evaluation
edge_cases.example: a provider model update quietly lowering accuracy
edge_cases.detection_method: trigger re-eval on every version change and watch baseline drift

edge_cases.trigger: input exceeds the reliable context window
edge_cases.failure_mode: silent truncation drops instructions or facts
edge_cases.example: a long document truncated so the question is cut
edge_cases.detection_method: detect when input length approaches the window and check for dropped content

edge_cases.trigger: an irreversible high-risk decision is fully automated
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible harm with no human checkpoint or accountable owner
edge_cases.example: auto-issuing irreversible refunds or account deletions
edge_cases.detection_method: verify high-risk/irreversible decision classes route to a named reviewer

edge_cases.trigger: only aggregate metrics are reported for a people-affecting system
edge_cases.failure_mode: subgroup harm hidden behind average accuracy
edge_cases.example: good overall accuracy while one group is systematically rejected
edge_cases.detection_method: disaggregate metrics by group and compare

workflow.objective: decide if an LLM fits and define the task and its guarantees

acceptance_tests: a non-LLM baseline is named and compared
do-not-use conditions stated
workflow.do_first_because: fit triage is the highest-coupling root that every later choice inherits

workflow.objective: choose the adaptation path, grounding strategy, and tools
acceptance_tests: path matches the knowledge profile
grounding accounts for cutoff and context limits
workflow.do_first_because: adaptation and grounding shape every downstream eval, cost, and safety choice

workflow.objective: assess hallucination, brittleness, overconfidence, and bias risks
acceptance_tests: fabrication cost rated and grounding set
brittleness and calibration tested
bias tested across groups
workflow.do_first_because: failure modes must be known before eval thresholds and review routing are set

workflow.objective: design a task-relevant, contamination-controlled evaluation and interpret scores
acceptance_tests: eval task matches production task
scores interpreted with limits
contamination assessed
exit_criteria: eval plan approved and quality floor set
workflow.do_first_because: a trustworthy quality floor must exist before cost tradeoffs and release

workflow.objective: set the cost/latency/quality operating point against the quality floor
entry_criteria: eval plan approved and quality floor set
acceptance_tests: a measured quality floor is defined first
cost/latency measured against it
workflow.do_first_because: cost cannot be traded against quality before the floor is measured

workflow.objective: design guardrails, injection defense, and assess alignment/refusal behavior
acceptance_tests: unsafe output classes filtered
injection tested
refusal behavior checked
workflow.do_first_because: safety controls must precede any production exposure

workflow.objective: govern data handling, human-review routing, and accountability
acceptance_tests: data minimized and terms acceptable
high-risk decisions route to a human
owners and rollback defined
workflow.do_first_because: data and accountability governance must be set before launch

workflow.objective: run end-to-end validation and human review before release
acceptance_tests: eval thresholds met
guardrails and injection tests pass
high-risk paths reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: end-to-end validation and human sign-off must pass before any hard lock or launch

workflow.objective: deploy with monitoring for drift, regression, and cost/quality
acceptance_tests: live quality monitored vs baseline
version changes trigger re-eval
rollback path exists
workflow.do_first_because: monitoring must be live before traffic is trusted, to catch silent regression

workflow.objective: respond to drift, incidents, and version changes with re-eval and accountability
acceptance_tests: drift/incidents trigger re-eval
decisions are documented
accountability maintained
exit_criteria: iteration cycle closed for this change
workflow.do_first_because: continuous re-verification keeps trust valid as models and inputs change

dominance_rules.trigger: a deployment is wanted before high-risk failure modes are validated
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk or irreversible AI uses wait for failure-mode validation and human review
dominance_rules.required_action: block launch until validation and review pass
dominance_rules.example: refusing to ship an automated irreversible action without review

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is sequenced before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency precedence outranks raw value when ordering work
dominance_rules.example: settling fit before choosing an adaptation path

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise-looking number lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade unsupported values to heuristic with SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR
dominance_rules.example: labeling an estimate heuristic rather than observed without data

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is about to be locked before validation passes
dominance_rules.rule: QA and validation outrank locking and progress
dominance_rules.required_action: block the lock until acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: refusing to hard-lock before the eval passes

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision could be fully automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review outranks automation for high-risk or irreversible decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: route the decision to a human gate
dominance_rules.example: a person approves any irreversible account action

dominance_rules.trigger: a genuinely unsafe output class trades off against helpfulness
dominance_rules.rule: safety dominates for genuinely unsafe classes; helpfulness is preserved elsewhere
dominance_rules.required_action: filter unsafe classes; avoid over-blocking benign ones
dominance_rules.example: blocking harmful instructions while allowing safe questions

dominance_rules.trigger: sensitive data would be sent or trained for a capability gain
dominance_rules.rule: privacy and data minimization dominate capability gains for sensitive data
dominance_rules.required_action: minimize/redact or use a no-train path
dominance_rules.example: choosing a no-train endpoint over fine-tuning on PII

dominance_rules.trigger: a public benchmark rank conflicts with a task-relevant eval
dominance_rules.rule: the task-relevant eval dominates a public leaderboard when they disagree
dominance_rules.required_action: decide on the task-relevant eval, caveat the benchmark
dominance_rules.example: rejecting a high-leaderboard model that fails the real-task eval

dominance_rules.trigger: a fluent answer may be fabricated or stale
dominance_rules.rule: grounding and verification outrank fluent presentation for factual claims
dominance_rules.required_action: require grounding/verification where fabrication is costly
dominance_rules.example: verifying a cited source rather than trusting confident prose

dominance_rules.trigger: a local optimization would bypass validation or anti-rework order
dominance_rules.rule: anti-rework sequencing and validation outrank local optimization
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the validated order; do not skip gates for a local win
dominance_rules.example: not skipping the eval to ship a model faster

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle use-case fit before any adaptation or build work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: building for an ill-fit task is fully reworked or scrapped
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: path/prompt work begins before a fit decision
anti_rework_rules.example: starting RAG before confirming an LLM is even the right tool

anti_rework_rules.rule: assess failure modes before fixing eval thresholds and review routing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: thresholds set without failure modes are re-derived later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: eval thresholds set before hallucination/bias are rated
anti_rework_rules.example: setting an accuracy threshold before knowing fabrication cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix a trustworthy quality floor before trading cost against quality
blocked_until: eval plan approved and quality floor set
anti_rework_rules.rationale: cost cuts made before a floor get undone when quality fails
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: cost optimization begins with no measured floor
anti_rework_rules.example: shrinking the model before the eval defines the floor

anti_rework_rules.rule: check contamination before trusting a benchmark score
anti_rework_rules.rationale: decisions on leaked scores are reversed when leakage is found
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a benchmark score is acted on without provenance check
anti_rework_rules.example: selecting a model on a leaked benchmark and reverting later

anti_rework_rules.rule: decide grounding before relying on parametric knowledge for fresh facts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fixes for stale answers in production are costly retrofits
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: fresh facts answered from parametric memory
anti_rework_rules.example: discovering post-launch that recent facts were wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: stand up guardrails and injection defense before exposing tools to untrusted input
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a breach forces an emergency redesign of the tool surface
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tools with data access ship before injection testing
anti_rework_rules.example: an injection incident forcing tool permissions to be rebuilt

anti_rework_rules.rule: set data-handling policy before sending data to a provider
anti_rework_rules.rationale: data already sent cannot be recalled; rework is remediation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: sensitive data flows before a handling policy exists
anti_rework_rules.example: remediating a leak after PII was already trained on

anti_rework_rules.rule: route irreversible decisions to human review before automating them
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible automated harm cannot be undone, only compensated
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an irreversible decision is automated with no review gate
anti_rework_rules.example: auto-deleting data with no human checkpoint

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass end-to-end validation and sign-off before any hard lock or launch
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before validation forces re-opening locked artifacts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock or launch precedes validation sign-off
anti_rework_rules.example: launching before the validation gate passes

anti_rework_rules.rule: stand up monitoring before trusting production traffic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: silent regression discovered late costs more than monitoring up front
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: traffic is trusted before monitoring is live
anti_rework_rules.example: noticing a quality drop only after user complaints
